hockey_player.evidence: All essential hockey equipment is present and in the correct anatomical locations, though the stick becomes hard to see when downscaled.

toy.evidence: The oversized heads, stubby limbs, lack of joints, and simple flat shading strongly convey a plastic toy figure.

answer.best_row: The top row reads best because the upright poses clearly show the silhouette and the large numbers on the back aid identification.
changes: stick thickness 2px -> 4px to maintain visibility at a distance
helmet cage bars 1px -> 3px and reduce number of bars to simplify
skate blade color dark grey -> light silver to separate from shadows
worst: The stick shaft is too thin and vanishes completely in the downscaled view.
The helmet cage is too complex and thin, turning into visual noise at a distance.
The sliding pose in the bottom middle breaks the silhouette and makes the legs unreadable.
works: The chunky proportions and oversized heads perfectly capture the toy aesthetic.
The high-contrast, saturated orange and blue jersey colors pop well against the ice.
The large, bold white numbers on the back are highly readable.
